lawyer:
Mr. Md. Shamsul Huda, Advocate ------ For Petitioners
Mr. Abdur Razzaque Miah, Advocate ------ For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Abdul Hai Mina and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Shaik Bazlur Rahman and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J: This rule is directed against the order dated 18.6.1987 passed by the Assistant Judge, Lohagarah in Misc. Case No. 51 of 1987 by which the ex-parte decree dated 11.4.1979 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Jessore in Title Suit No. 91 of 1970 subsequently re-numbered as Title Suit No. 159 of 1987 was set aside. 

 2. Relevant facts, in short, for the purpose of the case are that the petitioners as plaintiffs filed a suit in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Jessore, being Title Suit No. 91 of 1970 which was subsequently re-numbered as Title Suit No. 159 of 1987 on transfer for a declaration that the compromise decree passed in Title Suit No. 152 of 1969 is fraudulent collusive illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Eventually the said suit was decreed ex-parte on 11.4.79. Thereafter defendant opposite party No. 1 Shaikh Bazlur Rahman filed on 11.5.1979 an application under Order 9 Rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the aforesaid ex-parte decree on the ground that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the suit was taken up for ex-parte disposal whereupon Misc. Case No. 69 of 1979 was started. Unfortunately, the said case was dismissed for default on 23.11.82. Thereafter defendant opposite party No. 1 filed an application for review under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure whereupon Misc. Case No. 153 of 1983 was started. The aforesaid review application was filed for setting aside the order dated 23.11.82 by which Misc. Case No. 69 of 1979 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was dismissed for default. In the meantime, because of the creation of the Court of Assistant Judge at Lohagarah as a result of reorganisation of the Courts the case was transferred to the Court of the Assistant Judge. Lohagarah for disposal and the learned Assistant Judge, Lohagara by his order dated 16.6.1986 dismissed Misc. Case 'No. 153 of 1983 for default. Thereafter on 13.4.87 defendant opposite party No. 1 filed an application before the Assistant Judge, Lohagarah under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 16.6.86 for setting aside the dismissal of Misc. Case No. 156 of 1987 for default on the ground that he had no knowledge about the transfer of the case from Jessore to the Court of the Assistant Judge, Lohagara and no notice was given to him on the transfer of the aforesaid case from Jessore to Lohagarah. 

 3. The learned Assistant Judge by his order dated 3.5.87 allowed the aforesaid application of the defendant opposite party under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure setting aside the order of dismissal of Misc. Case No. 156 of 1985 for default and restored Misc. Case No. 156 of 1985 to its original file and number fixing 20.5.87 for steps. Thereafter by order dated 3.6.87 the learned Assistant Judge allowed Misc. Case No. 156 of 1985 under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and set aside the order dated 23.11.82 dismissing Misc. Case No. 69 of 1979 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, Subsequently, by the impugned order dated 18.6.1987 the learned Assistant Judge allowed the case under Order 9 rule 13 Of the Code of Civil Procedure and set aside the ex-parte decree dated 11.4.1979. Being aggrieved by, this order the petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. Mr. Shumsul Huda the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the learned Assistant Judge evidently erred in law in setting aside the order dated 16.6.86 and restoring Misc. Case No. 156 of 1985 to its original file and number acting under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure behind the back and beyond the knowledge of the petitioners and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Assistant Judge also erred in law in allowing Misc. Case No. 156 of 1985 by order dated 3.6.87 whereby the dismissal of the case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for default on 23.11.82 was set aside without hearing the petitioners and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that in view of the fact the impugned order dated 18.6.87 setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 11.4.79 in Title Suit No. 91 of 1970 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 159 of 1987 was made beyond the knowledge of the petitioners without al fording them any opportunity of being, the same is liable to be set aside in the interest of justice. 

 6. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has placed before me the impugned Order as well as the application under Order 9 Rule 13 read with section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure whereupon Misc. Case No. 69 of 1979 was started. This application has been marked as Annexure 'B' to the petition the order dated 23.11.82 dismissing Misc. Case No. 69 of 1979 for default, the application of defendant opposite party No. 1 under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for review of the order dated 23.11.82 whereupon Misc. Case No. 156 of 1985 was started the order dated 16.6.86 by which Misc. Case No. 56 of 1985 for review was dismissed for default. the order dated 23.5.87 by which the learned Assistant Judge, Lohagarah allowed the case of the defendant opposite party No. 1 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure after setting aside the order of dismissal dated 16.6.86 and restoring Misc. Case No. 156 of 1985 to its original file and number fixing 20.5.87 for steps, the order dated 3.6.87 by which the order dated. 23.11.87 dismissing the defendants case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Misc. Case No. 69 of 1979 was set aside and the original Misc. Case was revived. From these it is clearly found that the learned Assistant Judge, Lohagarah by his order dated 16.6.86 dismissed Misc. Case No. (Review Case) 156 of 1985 for default for failing to take necessary steps. There is nothing on record to indicate that after Misc. Case No. 56 of 1985 was transferred from Jessore to the Court of the Assistant Judge, Lohagara, the parties were informed of the transfer of the said case from Jessore to Lohagara. In the facts and circumstances of the case it cannot be said with any amount of certainty that the petitioners of Misc. Case No.156 of 1985 had any knowledge about the transfer of his case from Jessore to Lohagara requiring him to take necessary steps for want of which Misc. Case No. 156 of 1985 was dismissed for default. It also appears that the learned Assistant Judge on the application of the defendant opposite party No. 1 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the dismissal of the case for default ex-parte set aside the dismissal order dated 16.6.86 without serving any notice upon the petitioners and re-stored Misc. Case No.56 of 1985 to its original file and number behend their back and beyond their knowledge. It is also evident that by the subsequent order dated 3.6.87 the learned Assistant Judge, Lohagara set aside the order dated 3.6.87 setting aside the order dated 23.11.82 by which Misc. Case No. 69 of 1979 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was set aside and the case was re-stored to its original file and number. This order was also passed in the absence of the plaintiff-petitioners. There is nothing on record to show that they had any opportunity to have their say in the matter. Similarly the impugned order dated 18.6.87 allowing Misc. Case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure after setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 11.4.79 was passed ex-parte without affording any opportunity to the plaintiff-petitioners of being heard. 

 8. It is well-settled that when an order either contested or ex-parte is passed by any Court determining a matter before him a valuable tight accrues to the opposite party and that legal right cannot be taken away without affording such party an opportunity of being heard. In our case under review, the learned Assistant Judge merrily went on passing one order after another in the absence of the opposite parties taking away their valuable legal right without ensuring that necessary opportunities were given to them to have their say in the relevant matters. Such a course is never contemplated in law as it clearly militates against the principle of natural justice. The unfortunate procedure adopted by the learned Assistant Judge is not only arbitrary and illegal but also patently injudicious. It is thus found that the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order dated 16.6.86 in dismissing Misc. Case No. 156 of 1985 for default in a most, casual manner. The order dated 3.5.87 allowing the application of the defendant-opposite party No. 1 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is equally arbitrary and illegal. Similarly the order dated 3.6.87 by which the learned Assistant Judge set aside the order dated 23.11.82 passed in Misc. Case No. 69 of 1979 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the plaintiffs-petitioners is also illegal and arbitrary and the same is the fate of the impugned order dated 18.6.87 by which the ex-parte decree dated 11.4.1979 was set aside, without affording the plaintiff-petitioners any opportunity of being heard. 

 9. All these ultimately led to the passing of the impugned order dated 18.6.87 clearly indicating securing the non-application of a judicial mind by the learned Assistant Judge into the facts and circumstances and the law bearing on the subject and the same has occasioned failure of justice. In the facts and circumstances of the case, I am constrained to hold that orders dated 16.6.86. 3.5.87 and 3.6.87 passed in Misc. Case No. 165 of 1985 are illegal and arbitrary and the same cannot the allowed to stand in the interest of justice. I am also constrained to hold that the learned Assistant Judge. Lohagara clearly erred in law in passing the impugned order dated 18.6.87 in Misc. Case No. 51 of 1987 in setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 11.4.79 behind the back and beyond the knowledge of the petitioners and accordingly the said order is liable to be set aside. The submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners merit consideration and the same are accordingly sustained.
